name: Whey (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Whey [Milk and milk products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 171282 (Whey, sweet, fluid; SR Legacy), macronutrients, sugars, amino acids, fatty acids, minerals, vitamins, cholesterol
21 CFR 184.1979 (Whey standard), sweet-whey lactose 46-52 g/L, protein 6-9 g/L, titratable acidity <=0.16% as lactic
J Dairy Sci invited review, Acid whey trends and health benefits, S0022-0302(20)31055-9, sweet vs acid whey lactic acid
J Dairy Sci, role of sodium in salty taste of permeate, S0022-0302(14)00494-9, whey/permeate organic acids (lactic, citric, orotic)
Milk citrate partition (~1.75-2.0 g/L, ~90% soluble) into whey, cheesescientist.com; PMC9457946
provenance.curation_notes: Sweet (rennet/cheese) fluid whey. Dominant carbon/energy source is lactose (~5.1 g/100g, ~150 mM); the growth-critical additions over the FooDB profile are the organic acids, citric acid (~0.16 g/100g, ~8 mM, inherited from milk citrate) and lactic acid (low in sweet whey but the defining acid of acid/yogurt whey, up to ~16x higher). Secondary N sources are soluble whey proteins (beta-lactoglobulin, alpha-lactalbumin) and their amino acids; minerals dominated by K > Na > Ca > P; riboflavin-rich
curation_added: citric acid (~0.16 g/100g), dominant native whey organic acid, absent from FooDB
lactic acid (~0.05 g/100g sweet whey; up to ~1.6 g/L, far higher in acid whey)
orotic acid and acetic acid (characteristic dairy organic acids)
lactose given an explicit quantitative amount (5.14 g/100g) as the dominant fermentable sugar
full protein-derived amino-acid profile with amounts

curation_removed.name: Sucrose C12H22O11
curation_removed.reason: Whey contains no sucrose; the sole sugar is lactose. FooDB mis-assignment.

curation_removed.name: Nickel
curation_removed.reason: Non-nutritive trace/contaminant metal, not a defining whey nutrient.

curation_removed.name: Co2+
curation_removed.reason: Elemental cobalt is present only within vitamin B12; standalone Co2+ is non-nutritive FooDB noise (B12 retained).

curation_removed.name: Molybdate
curation_removed.reason: Ultratrace, unquantified; not a growth-relevant whey nutrient.

curation_removed.name: (R)-Oxypeucedanin
curation_removed.reason: Plant furanocoumarin (parsnip/citrus); biologically implausible in dairy whey. FooDB predicted noise.

curation_removed.name: epsilon-Polylysine
curation_removed.reason: Microbial-fermentation preservative, not a native whey constituent. FooDB noise.

curation_removed.name: (E)-2-Phenyl-2-butenal
curation_removed.reason: Trace flavor aldehyde/volatile, not a growth nutrient.

curation_removed.name: (±)-erythro-Isoleucine
curation_removed.reason: Non-physiological isoleucine stereoisomer artifact; real isoleucine already listed as L-isoleucine.

curation_removed.name: 24,25-Dihydroxyvitamin D3
curation_removed.reason: Predicted trace vitamin-D metabolite, not a measured growth nutrient of whey.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all divides components by (components + unresolved ingredients). It counts pipeline-derived components as covered, so it is not a measure of how much of the source's own ingredient list was captured. pct_covered_source divides source-stated components by (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components), which is that measure. Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
